findings.name: measurement_trust
findings.detail: Q_max was measured with autoscaling suspended, capacity pinned to (1,), and no container queue bound, so it reads as one instance's own limit

findings.name: curve_repeatability
findings.detail: Q_max 50 came from a single ladder pass, so whether it is repeatable was never established — a 0% spread across one run is not an agreement
findings.recommendation: re-run `tts-bench qmax --runs 2` or more to get a spread

findings.name: slo_budget
findings.detail: W_max 2.93s = 3.0s SLO - 0.066s p95 service — derived, not configured, so the queue allowance cannot drift away from the promise it is spending

findings.name: invocation_ceiling
findings.detail: a queued request finishes in 3.0s worst case (W_max 2.9s + p95 service 0.07s), inside the 60s SageMaker invocation ceiling

findings.name: queue_depth
findings.detail: queue_max_depth 50 is the measured Q_max, bracketed from above. The SLO's wait budget independently implies about 48 (W_max 2.93s / S 0.061s); past the bound a request cannot reach first byte in time, so it is refused rather than served late

findings.name: threshold_units
findings.detail: scaling_target_value 37.50 = C_scale_max 37.50 x 1.00, the measured ratio of ConcurrentRequestsPerModel / Maximum to client mean in-flight at the nearest rung. The converted figure is what deploys; the occupancy is what was measured

findings.name: surge_survival
findings.detail: holding C_scale_max 37.50 of Q_max 50 is 97.4% utilization on a single-server queue, and a replacement takes 320s to arrive — so P(the queue reaches Q_max before then) is 100%, past the 10% line. The 1.25x surge ratio reserves queue slots, which is a stock; surviving a surge is about drain rate, which is a flow, and at this utilization there is very little of it left
findings.recommendation: scale out earlier than the simple rule (a smaller share of Q_max), shorten T_total, or hold standing headroom in instances

findings.name: scale_in_safety
findings.detail: scale-in is only stable from 3 instances up: removing one of N multiplies each survivor's concurrency by N/(N-1), which must stay under 1.50 (= C_scale_max 37.50 / C_scale_min 25.00). This plan's floor is 1, so a 2->1 scale-in leaves the survivors at 50.00
findings.recommendation: raise --min-floor to 3, or accept the flap that the scale-in cooldown damps but does not remove

findings.name: fleet_cost
findings.detail: reserving headroom for a 1.25x surge costs 1.3x a fleet scaled at Q_max (9 instances at C_scale_max 37.50 against 7 at Q_max); on-demand rates, so an upper bound

findings.name: provision_stage
findings.detail: T_total 320s, of which 181s (56%) is EC2 provisioning and image pull — a property of this account's spare capacity, not of the configuration. A reserved-capacity account, where placement is guaranteed, will differ on that part and only that part. Of that, 60s is the policy's detection lag, which the force-desired trigger bypasses and so is BOUNDED from the deployed alarm's periods and cooldown rather than measured.

provenance.note: Q_max at the 3000ms p95 TTFAB SLO on response-stream, autoscaling frozen; T_total measured, trigger=force-desired; 260s measured + 60s policy lag bounded from the deployed alarm, not measured
supplied as a CLI argument; no production traffic to measure

config_block:
"kokoro-82m": ModelEndpointConfig(
        model_name="kokoro-82m",
        instance_type="ml.g5.xlarge",
        min_instances=1,  # trough 10 rps; 3 is the smallest safe for scale-in
        max_instances=9,  # peak 5000 rps
        scaling_target_value=37.500,  # C_scale_max 37.50 x 1.00 CW units; = (1-h) x Q_max 50 at h=0.25
        scale_in_threshold=25.000,  # C_scale_min 25.00 x 1.00; = (1-2h) x Q_max, one surge of excess headroom
        ttfab_slo_ms=3000,  # end-to-end promise; W_max 2.93s + p95 service 0.07s fits the 60s invocation ceiling
        queue_max_depth=50,  # = Q_max: past it a request cannot reach first byte inside the 3.0s SLO
        scale_out_cooldown_s=30,  # short: target tracking adds one instance at a time
        scale_in_cooldown_s=960,  # long: removed capacity costs a full 320s to replace
    ),
alarm_threshold: FirstChunkLatencyP95 alarm: 65ms (p95 TTFAB at one outstanding request). NOT the 3000ms SLO: this alarm watches service time on an instance already serving, where a request has spent none of its queue allowance.
